newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela says South Africa ready for Central Africa role.
newsitem.headline: Mandela says South Africa ready for Central Africa role.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela said on Thursday South Africa was prepared to play a role in troubled central Africa, but he did not say what form this might take.

The South African president, who has been reluctant to be drawn into the crisis in the Great Lakes region, said he had discussed the situation there with Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni by telephone on Thursday afternoon.

Mandela told state television their conversation had not focused on specifics in the region, where more than a million refugees are caught up in fighting between ethnic Tutsi rebels and the army in eastern Zaire.
"....We are ready to play a part, provided that this coincides with our own law and that we have the capacity to perform what we are required to do," he said.

Deputy Foreign Affairs Minister Aziz Pahad told the television that South Africa was not ready for peacekeeping operations, but needed to "start preparing to be ready for any eventual involvement of this sort".
Fighting between Zairean troops and the Tutsi rebels, known as Banyamulenge, raged on Thursday in eastern Zaire near the Rwandan border.

Mandela has been cool on U.S. proposals for an intervention force for deployment in African hot-spots, saying the Pretoria government could only support it if it was formed by the United Nations or the Organisation of African Unity.
His government has come in for criticism at home for agreeing to sell arms to Rwanda while the situation in central Africa is so unstable.
There are about 1.1 million Hutu refugees in the region, many of whom fled Rwanda fearing justice and reprisals after the massacre of up to one million ethnic Tutsis and moderate Hutus in 1994.

South Africa's last white government, ousted by Mandela's African National Congress in the country's first all-race polls two and a half years ago, sold weapons to the Hutu factions responsible for the Rwandan genocide.
